Defensive leadership was evident in Utilities, and Energy also outperformed, while Technology & Communications and Healthcare occupied the bottom of the leaderboard. [...] Technology and healthcare stocks were the weakest areas of the market in Thursday afternoon trading, with software names and select life sciences companies weighing on sector performance. The sharpest pressure appeared in Technology & Communications, where large-cap software stocks pulled the group lower, while Healthcare also lagged on outsized declines in individual constituents. Stocks capped a choppy day of trading on Wall Street with more losses Thursday after an early big tech rally faded and a healthcare sector pullback led the market lower.

The Standard & Poor’s 500 index fell 0.4%, its third straight decline. The benchmark index, which is just below the record high it set on Monday, notched a 2.2% gain for the month of July and is up 7.8% so far this year.

The Dow Jones industrial average lost 0.7%, and the Nasdaq composite closed less than 0.1% lower. [...] Earnings remain a key focus outside of the technology sector in what has been a heavy week so far for corporate financial results. CVS Health fell 0.3% after it topped Wall Street expectations for the second quarter and raised its full-year forecast again.
